_hinweis: Vocabulary step on /teachers/lesson and /lesson: for each A1 word field in kursinhalte.json (bloecke[].wortschatz, keys must match exactly) a task for the learners and its words. A word that is a lemma of the A1 list (src/content/lexicon/a1.json) gets its a/an/some, plural and example sentence from there; a noun the list does not have may be written with its article ("a menu", "some cash"); phrases without an entry (Hello!, letters) are shown as written here. Word fields without an entry only show the general task.

Greetings.aufgabe: Walk around the room. Say hello to three people, ask how they are and say goodbye – once friendly, once formal.

Countries.aufgabe: Ask your partner: “Where are you from?” – “I'm from …”. Show the country on a map or on your phone.

Languages.aufgabe: Ask each other: “What languages do you speak?” Everyone says two languages. Write all the languages of the class on the board.

The alphabet.aufgabe: Spell your first name and your surname. Your partner writes them down and reads them back.

Numbers.aufgabe: Count round the class to 20, then in tens to 100. In pairs, dictate three phone numbers to each other.

Address.aufgabe: Ask each other: “Where do you live?” Write down your partner's address: number, street, town and postcode.

Email.aufgabe: Dictate an email address to your partner. Your partner writes it down and reads it back.

Forms.aufgabe: In pairs, fill in a form for each other: ask, listen, write.

Family.aufgabe: Draw your family tree and explain it to your partner: “This is my mother …”

Married, single ….aufgabe: Ask politely: “Are you married?” Answer for a person you invent.

Describing people.aufgabe: Describe a person in the class. The others guess who it is.

Rooms.aufgabe: Draw your flat or house. Show your partner around: “This is the kitchen …”

Furniture.aufgabe: Say what is in your living room. Your partner draws it.

Colours.aufgabe: Find something in the room for every colour and say: “The bag is blue.”

big / small / light.aufgabe: Describe your room with three adjectives. Your partner says if their room is the same.

Food.aufgabe: Write your shopping list for the weekend. Read it to your partner.

Drinks.aufgabe: Ask three people: “What do you drink in the morning?” Write down the answers.

Containers (a bottle of, a packet of).aufgabe: Play shop: one person sells, one person buys. Use “a bottle of”, “a packet of”, “a kilo of”.

Prices.aufgabe: Write prices on cards. Your partner asks: “How much is it?” and you read the price.

Daily routine.aufgabe: Tell your partner about your morning: “I get up at seven. Then I …”

Times of the day.aufgabe: Say what you do at each time of the day. Your partner says one thing for each, too.

Days of the week.aufgabe: Ask each other: “What do you do on Monday?” Make a plan for the week together.

Hobbies.aufgabe: Ask three people: “What do you do in your free time?” Find one hobby you share.
woerter: What do you do in your free time?

Sport.aufgabe: Mime a sport. The others guess it: “Do you play football?”

Music.aufgabe: Ask your partner about music: What do they like? Do they play an instrument?

Weekend.aufgabe: Plan a weekend together: Saturday morning, Saturday afternoon, Sunday.

Places in town.aufgabe: Draw a small map of your town. Your partner asks: “Is there a bank?”

Directions.aufgabe: Use the map. Explain the way from the station to the bank. Your partner follows it with a finger.

Transport.aufgabe: Ask three people: “How do you get to work or school?” Count the answers.

Tickets.aufgabe: Role play at the ticket office: buy a ticket to London.

The body.aufgabe: Play “Simon says”: one person says a body part, everyone touches it.

Illnesses.aufgabe: Mime an illness. The others guess: “Have you got a headache?”

At the doctor's.aufgabe: Role play: phone the doctor's surgery and make an appointment.
woerter: I'd like to make an appointment.
How long have you had it?

The chemist's.aufgabe: Role play at the chemist's: say what is wrong and ask for something for it.
woerter: Have you got something for a cold?

Weekend activities.aufgabe: Ask your partner: “What did you do at the weekend?” Tell the class one thing.

Time words: yesterday, last week, ago.aufgabe: Make a timeline on the board: today, yesterday, last week, two days ago. Everyone adds one sentence.

Jobs.aufgabe: Mime a job. The others guess: “Are you a teacher?”

Workplaces.aufgabe: Say where people work: “A teacher works in a school.” Your partner names another job.

Working hours.aufgabe: Ask each other: “When do you start work? When do you finish?” Write down the times.
woerter: I work from nine to five.

Clothes.aufgabe: Describe what a person in the class is wearing. The others guess who it is.

Sizes.aufgabe: Role play in a clothes shop: ask for a different size.
woerter: Have you got this in a medium?

In the shop.aufgabe: Role play: you buy a jumper. The other person is the shop assistant.

Months.aufgabe: Line up by birthday, January to December. Everyone says their month.

Celebrations.aufgabe: Tell your partner about a celebration in your country: When is it? What do people do?

Invitations.aufgabe: Write a short invitation to a party. Your partner says yes or no and gives a reason.

Bank.aufgabe: Role play at the bank: open an account or ask about your card.
woerter: I'd like to open an account.

Post office.aufgabe: Role play at the post office: send a parcel to another country.
woerter: How much is a stamp for Spain?
I'd like to send this parcel.

Appointments.aufgabe: Make an appointment with your partner: find a day and a time that works for both of you.

Opening times.aufgabe: Ask your partner about the opening times of a shop, the library and the bank. Write them down.
